─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IP COUNSEL DILIGENCE MEMO — DEAL STRUCTURE, IP CHAIN-OF-TITLE,
OSS COMPLIANCE & ASSIGNMENT STEP-PLAN
Prepared by: IP Counsel
Date: 2026-10-03
Classification: PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

SCOPE NOTE
This memo addresses the IP-dimension of deal structure selection, tax-election mechanics as they interact with IP ownership, chain-of-title validation, open-source software (OSS) compliance, and the full assignment/covenant step-plan for a generic acquisition transaction. Where target-specific facts are unavailable, conservative assumptions and bracketed placeholders are used; counsel should substitute confirmed data before execution.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PART I — DEAL STRUCTURE ANALYSIS (IP LENS)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

IP-001 STRUCTURE ELECTION: ASSET PURCHASE vs. STOCK PURCHASE vs. MERGER

A. Asset Purchase
   • IP ADVANTAGE: Acquirer takes only enumerated IP assets; excludes unknown encumbrances not disclosed.
   • IP RISK: Each patent, trademark, copyright, domain, and trade-secret record requires a separate recordable assignment instrument. Failure to record with USPTO, USCO, WIPO, and foreign registries within statutory windows creates gap in chain-of-title.
   • TAX INTERACTION: §338(h)(10) or §336(e) elections permit deemed-asset treatment in a stock deal; if a true asset deal is used, Acquirer obtains a stepped-up basis in IP assets (§197 amortisation over 15 years for acquired intangibles).
   • RECOMMENDATION: Asset purchase preferred where target IP portfolio has unresolved employee/contractor assignment gaps (see IP-004) or where OSS contamination is suspected (see IP-008 et seq.).

B. Stock Purchase (no §338 election)
   • IP ADVANTAGE: IP title transfers automatically with entity ownership; no individual IP re-registration required.
   • IP RISK: Acquirer inherits all latent IP liabilities — unassigned employee inventions, pre-existing OSS licence violations, prior ownership disputes, encumbrances under loan facilities (IP as collateral).
   • RECOMMENDATION: Acceptable only after full IP diligence clears chain-of-title and OSS audit (Parts II–IV).

C. Forward/Reverse Triangular Merger
   • Forward Triangular: Target merges into Acquirer subsidiary; IP vests in subsidiary by operation of law. Some IP licence agreements contain "change of control" or "assignment without consent" anti-assignment clauses — these are triggered.
   • Reverse Triangular: Acquisition subsidiary merges into Target; Target survives. Anti-assignment clauses generally not triggered (entity identity preserved). Preferred structure where Target holds material third-party IP licences with anti-assignment language.
   • RECOMMENDATION: Default to reverse triangular merger unless tax counsel requires otherwise; conduct anti-assignment clause audit (IP-006) pre-signing.

IP-002 §338(h)(10) / §336(e) ELECTION MECHANICS (IP INTERACTION)

   • A §338(h)(10) election (S-corp or consolidated subsidiary target) or §336(e) election (standalone C-corp) causes a deemed asset sale for tax purposes. For IP purposes:
     – Target is treated as selling all IP assets at fair market value; Acquirer obtains stepped-up §197 basis.
     – A "deemed bill of sale" for IP is not recorded; however, the IP remains titled in Target (now surviving entity or merged into Acquirer's sub). No separate USPTO/WIPO recordation is needed.
     – Allocation under §1060 / Form 8594 must assign FMV to Class VI (§197 intangibles — patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, customer lists, goodwill) and Class VII (going concern). IP Counsel must supply FMV support schedule to tax counsel for each IP asset category.
   • ACTION: IP Counsel to deliver IP Asset Valuation Schedule (Schedule A to this memo) identifying all registered IP, pending applications, and trade secrets with estimated FMV ranges for §1060 allocation within [10] business days of signing.

IP-003 ROLLOVER EQUITY & IP COVENANTS

   • Seller shareholders receiving rollover equity (typically 10–40% of total consideration) must execute:
     (a) Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement (IPAA) — confirming all IP created pre-closing vests in Target/Acquirer; no retained licence.
     (b) Non-Competition / Non-Solicitation Agreement — protecting Acquirer's IP position post-closing.
     (c) Invention Assignment and Confidentiality Agreement (IACA) — if rolling employees/founders continue post-closing.
   • Rollover equity mechanics (LLC units, restricted stock, or profits interests) must confirm that vesting does not create a §83(b) issue that inadvertently triggers a deemed contribution of IP to a partnership/LLC taxed entity — consult tax counsel on §721 vs. §83 interaction.

IP-004 EARNOUT MECHANICS — IP MILESTONE TRIGGERS

   • If earnout consideration is tied to IP milestones (e.g., patent grant, FDA regulatory exclusivity, software release), the following protections are required:
     (a) Acquirer must covenant not to abandon, allow to lapse, or materially amend the relevant IP applications/registrations during the earnout period without Seller consent.
     (b) Define "Patent Grant" precisely — first allowed claim in any jurisdiction, or specifically USPTO grant; specify minimum claim scope threshold to prevent Acquirer from narrowing claims to defeat earnout.
     (c) OSS licence change covenants: Acquirer must not re-license core products under copyleft licence (GPL/AGPL) during earnout without Seller approval, as doing so could destroy commercial IP value and defeat earnout targets.
     (d) Earnout dispute resolution: IP-specific disputes (claim scope, inventorship) to be resolved by neutral patent attorney arbitrator (not general commercial arbitrator) within 60 days.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PART II — CHAIN-OF-TITLE VALIDATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

IP-005 EMPLOYEE & CONTRACTOR ASSIGNMENT AUDIT

   • STATUS: [PENDING — no target materials provided; standard findings below apply as presumptive framework]
   • REVIEW REQUIRED:
     (a) All employment agreements signed by current and former employees who contributed to material IP — confirm IACA signed at or before commencement of employment.
     (b) All independent contractor agreements — confirm work-for-hire language (§101 Copyright Act) AND separate written assignment clause (work-for-hire doctrine does not apply to patents; assignment clause is mandatory).
     (c) Founder IP assignments — confirm all founders assigned all pre-incorporation IP to Target entity; check for any founder who departed prior to IP recording.
     (d) University/prior employer conflicts — confirm no Bayh-Dole obligations, no prior employer ownership claims, no academic IP disclosure obligations outstanding.
   • GAP REMEDY: For any identified assignment gap, obtain retroactive Confirmatory Patent Assignment / Confirmatory Copyright Assignment before closing. If gap party is unavailable or uncooperative, Acquirer must obtain representations, indemnities, and escrow holdback sized to risk.

IP-006 THIRD-PARTY LICENCE ANTI-ASSIGNMENT AUDIT

   • Review all inbound IP licences (technology licences, font licences, SaaS platform agreements, data licences, SDK/API licences) for:
     (a) Express anti-assignment clauses ("shall not be assigned without prior written consent").
     (b) Change-of-control provisions triggering termination or consent rights.
     (c) Most-favoured-nation or exclusivity provisions that may be affected by merger.
   • CLASSIFICATION:
     – Tier 1 (Mission-Critical): Licences without which core product cannot operate. Consent must be obtained pre-closing. Failure = closing condition failure.
     – Tier 2 (Material): Licences affecting significant revenue line. Use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain consent; closing condition waivable by Acquirer.
     – Tier 3 (Non-Material): Commercially available licences easily replaced. Notify licensor post-closing per standard procedure.
   • REVERSE TRIANGULAR PREFERENCE: As noted in IP-001(C), reverse triangular merger preserves Target's legal identity and generally avoids triggering anti-assignment clauses. Confirm with licence counsel for each Tier 1 licence whether merger constitutes "assignment" under applicable governing law.

IP-007 REGISTERED IP STATUS CHECK

   • Confirm for each registered IP asset:
     (a) PATENTS: USPTO/WIPO assignment database — chain from inventors to assignee is unbroken and recorded. Maintenance fees current. No terminal disclaimers creating problematic co-dependency. No inter partes review (IPR) or ex parte reexamination pending.
     (b) TRADEMARKS: USPTO/EUIPO/national registries — registered in name of Target entity (not individual founder). Renewal deadlines and Statement of Use filings current. No pending oppositions or cancellations.
     (c) COPYRIGHTS: USCO registration for key software works, marketing materials, published works. Registration pre-dates any known infringement claim (prerequisite for statutory damages).
     (d) DOMAIN NAMES: WHOIS registrant matches Target entity. Confirm auto-renewal enabled; no impending expiry within 12 months of closing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PART III — OSS USAGE & LICENCE COMPLIANCE AUDIT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

IP-008 OSS AUDIT METHODOLOGY

   • Tool-assisted scan required using one or more of: Black Duck (Synopsis), FOSSA, Snyk Open Source, or REUSE/SPDX tooling.
   • Scan scope: All source code repositories (production, staging, internal tools); compiled binaries; container images; firmware (if applicable).
   • Output required: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) in SPDX 2.3 or CycloneDX 1.5 format, listing every OSS component, version, declared licence, and detected licence.

IP-009 LICENCE CATEGORY RISK MATRIX

   CATEGORY A — PERMISSIVE (MIT, BSD-2, BSD-3, Apache-2.0, ISC):
   • No copyleft obligation. Distribution of modifications not required.
   • Notice/attribution obligations must be satisfied in product documentation / NOTICE file.
   • VERDICT: CLEAR subject to attribution compliance.

   CATEGORY B — WEAK COPYLEFT (LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, MPL-2.0, CDDL):
   • Copyleft limited to the OSS component itself; proprietary code linked dynamically generally not affected.
   • Static linking of LGPL code into proprietary binary may trigger copyleft over linked code — confirm linkage method.
   • VERDICT: REVIEW REQUIRED for each component; confirm dynamic vs. static linkage.

   CATEGORY C — STRONG COPYLEFT (GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0):
   • Any distribution of software incorporating GPL code must be under GPL; source code must be made available.
   • If Target distributes a product (not pure SaaS), and GPL code is incorporated in distributed binary: FLAGGED.
   • SaaS exception: GPL does not require source disclosure for server-side-only code (no distribution). Confirm product delivery model.
   • VERDICT: FLAG for distribution review; CLEAR for pure SaaS/internal use.

   CATEGORY D — NETWORK COPYLEFT (AGPL-3.0, EUPL, OSL):
   • Copyleft triggered by network use — even SaaS delivery of AGPL-licensed code requires source disclosure to users.
   • Any AGPL component in a commercial SaaS product: BLOCKED unless (i) commercial licence obtained from upstream vendor, or (ii) component is isolated in a separate service with no proprietary code intermingling, or (iii) component is removed before closing.
   • VERDICT: BLOCKED until remediation confirmed.

   CATEGORY E — PROPRIETARY/COMMERCIAL OSS (dual-licence models, BSL, SSPL):
   • Business Source Licence (BSL/BUSL): Commercial use restriction until "Change Date." Confirm Change Date and production use rights.
   • Server Side Public Licence (SSPL): Functionally similar to AGPL; treat as Category D.
   • Elastic Licence 2.0 (ELv2): Prohibits offering the software as a managed service. If Target offers such service: BLOCKED.
   • VERDICT: Case-by-case; confirm commercial use rights pre-closing.

IP-010 OSS REMEDIATION REQUIREMENTS (FLAGGED/BLOCKED ITEMS)

   • For each FLAGGED or BLOCKED component:
     (a) Identify all code paths that incorporate the component.
     (b) Options assessed in order of preference:
         (i)   Remove component entirely (replace with permissive-licensed equivalent or proprietary code).
         (ii)  Obtain commercial licence from upstream vendor (converts OSS obligation to contractual licence).
         (iii) Segregate component into isolated microservice/container with clean API boundary; confirm no proprietary code in same binary.
         (iv)  Open-source the affected module under a compatible licence (last resort; requires business approval).
     (c) Remediation must be confirmed by re-scan before closing. No BLOCKED items may remain at closing.

IP-011 OSS NOTICE & ATTRIBUTION COMPLIANCE

   • Confirm all required OSS licence notices (MIT copyright lines, Apache NOTICE files, BSD attributions) are included in:
     (a) Product documentation / About screen / CREDITS file.
     (b) Source code repository (LICENSES/ directory per REUSE Specification).
   • Failure to include notices is a copyright infringement even for permissive licences.
   • Deliverable: OSS Attribution Report (Schedule B) to be attached to Disclosure Schedule.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PART IV — IP ASSIGNMENT SCHEDULES & COVENANT DRAFTS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

IP-012 SCHEDULE OF TRANSACTION IP DOCUMENTS

   The following IP documents are to be executed at or prior to closing:

   DOC-1: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT AGREEMENT (BULK ASSET)
   Purpose: Transfers all Target IP assets to Acquirer (asset deal) or confirms vesting in surviving entity (merger).
   Key provisions:
   • Granting clause covering: patents (issued and pending), patent applications, utility models, trademarks (registered and unregistered), service marks, trade dress, copyrights (registered and unregistered), trade secrets, know-how, software, source code, object code, databases, domain names, social media handles, moral rights (waived to fullest extent permitted by law).
   • "Further Assurance" clause: Target/Seller to execute all additional documents required to record transfer in any jurisdiction within [30] days of Acquirer's request.
   • Power of Attorney: Limited power of attorney to Acquirer to execute recordal documents if Target/Seller fails to comply within [15] days of notice.
   • Schedule of Registered IP: Exhibit A listing all registered/applied-for IP by jurisdiction, registration/application number, and expiry/renewal date.

   DOC-2: CONFIRMATORY PATENT ASSIGNMENT (PER INVENTOR)
   Purpose: Fills chain-of-title gaps identified in IP-005; ensures each named inventor on each patent/application has assigned to Target and Target assigns to Acquirer.
   • Must be in recordable form for USPTO (notarised if required for foreign jurisdictions).
   • Covers past, present, and future claims arising from inventions conceived/reduced to practice during employment/engagement period.

   DOC-3: INVENTION ASSIGNMENT & CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENT (IACA)
   Purpose: Prospective assignment of IP by rolling employees and contractors post-closing.
   Key provisions:
   • Assignment of all inventions, works of authorship, and developments arising from employment/engagement.
   • Carve-out for prior inventions (Schedule of Prior Inventions required from each signatory).
   • Exclusion for inventions developed entirely on employee's own time without use of Acquirer resources, as required by applicable state law (California Labor Code §2870; Delaware §2872; Washington RCW 49.44.140; confirm jurisdiction).
   • Obligation to disclose all inventions to IP Counsel within [30] days of conception.

   DOC-4: TRANSITION SERVICES AGREEMENT — IP LICENCE BACK
   Purpose: In an asset deal, Target (as seller) may need a limited licence back to certain IP to wind down operations or fulfil outstanding customer contracts.
   Key provisions:
   • Non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free licence for [6–12] months post-closing.
   • Strict field-of-use and territory limitations.
   • Automatic termination; no renewal right.

   DOC-5: IP REPRESENTATIONS & WARRANTIES (R&W) SCHEDULE
   To be incorporated into the Purchase Agreement. Key reps:
   (a) Target owns or has valid licence to all IP used in the business.
   (b) All IP created by employees/contractors has been validly assigned to Target.
   (c) No IP is subject to any lien, pledge, security interest, or encumbrance not disclosed.
   (d) Target has not received written notice of any claim that it infringes a third party's IP.
   (e) All OSS is used in compliance with applicable licences (no BLOCKED items at closing).
   (f) No government funding was used in development of IP (Bayh-Dole representation).
   (g) No IP is subject to open-source licence that would require disclosure of Acquirer's proprietary code.
   (h) All personnel with access to trade secrets are bound by confidentiality obligations.

   DOC-6: IP INDEMNITY & ESCROW PROVISIONS
   • Indemnity basket / deductible: [1–2]% of purchase price for IP-related indemnity claims.
   • Cap: [20–30]% of purchase price for IP R&W breaches; [100]% for fraud or intentional misrepresentation.
   • Survival period: [36] months post-closing for general IP reps; [60] months for fundamental IP reps (ownership, no encumbrances).
   • R&W Insurance: If R&W insurance obtained, confirm IP exclusions in policy and size escrow holdback to cover excluded items.
   • Specific Indemnity: Seller to indemnify for any pre-closing OSS compliance failure, even if not discovered until post-closing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PART V — STEP PLAN (EXECUTION TIMELINE)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

IP-013 TRANSACTION STEP PLAN — IP WORKSTREAM

   PHASE 0: PRE-LETTER OF INTENT (T-minus 4 weeks)
   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Week -4: IP Counsel retained; NDA executed (confirm NDA covers trade secrets adequately; mutual preferred).
   Week -4: Target provides IP asset list, OSS component list, and employment/contractor agreement templates for preliminary review.
   Week -3: Preliminary OSS scan initiated on any code samples provided under NDA.
   Week -3: IP Counsel issues preliminary IP Risk Assessment memo to deal team.
   Week -2: Deal team determines preferred deal structure (asset/stock/merger) based on IP risk profile and tax counsel input.
   Week -2: LOI drafted; IP Counsel reviews IP-related LOI provisions (exclusivity, IP access during diligence, interim operating covenant re: IP maintenance).

   PHASE 1: SIGNING TO DILIGENCE LAUNCH (T=0, Signing of LOI)
   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Day 1–3:   Data room access granted. IP Counsel begins full diligence review:
              • Employment/contractor agreements — assignment gap analysis (IP-005).
              • Registered IP portfolio — USPTO/WIPO/EUIPO search (IP-007).
              • Third-party licence audit — anti-assignment clause mapping (IP-006).
   Day 1–5:   OSS audit initiated — Black Duck/FOSSA scan of full codebase (IP-008).
   Day 7:     Preliminary OSS SBOM delivered. IP Counsel triages Category D (AGPL/SSPL) findings.
   Day 10:    IP Counsel issues first diligence report identifying Tier 1 issues requiring immediate remediation.
   Day 14:    SBOM finalised; OSS Risk Report (Schedule B) delivered. Remediation plan agreed with Target.

   PHASE 2: DEFINITIVE AGREEMENT NEGOTIATION (T+2 to T+6 weeks)
   ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Week 3:    IP R&W schedule drafted (DOC-5); IP indemnity provisions negotiated (DOC-6).
   Week 3:    Anti-assignment consent letters sent to all Tier 1 licence counterparties (IP-006).
   Week 4:    Bulk IP Assignment Agreement drafted (DOC-1); Confirmatory Patent Assignments prepared for each gap inventor (DOC-2).
   Week 4:    IACA drafted for all rolling employees and key contractors (DOC-3).
   Week 5:    Tax counsel delivers §1060 allocation schedule; IP Counsel provides IP FMV support (IP-002).
   Week 5:    Definitive Agreement (Purchase Agreement / Merger Agreement) executed. IP Schedules attached as Disclosure Schedules.
   Week 6:    OSS remediation confirmed by re-scan. All BLOCKED items resolved.

   PHASE 3: PRE-CLOSING COVENANTS (Signing to Closing)
   ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Ongoing:   Target covenants:
              (a) Maintain all registered IP (pay maintenance fees, respond to office actions).
              (b) Not to abandon, license, encumber, or transfer any IP outside ordinary course without Acquirer consent.
              (c) Not to introduce new OSS components in Category C/D without IP Counsel approval.
              (d) Promptly notify Acquirer of any new IP claims, infringement notices, or ownership disputes.
   Closing-7: Tier 1 licence consents received and confirmed in writing.
   Closing-5: Confirmatory Patent Assignments signed by all identified gap inventors.
   Closing-3: IACA signed by all rolling employees.
   Closing-1: Final IP diligence bringdown certificate signed by Target.

   PHASE 4: CLOSING (T+8 to T+12 weeks, as applicable)
   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Closing Day: Deliverables exchange:
                • DOC-1 (Bulk IP Assignment) executed and delivered.
                • DOC-2 (Confirmatory Patent Assignments) executed and delivered.
                • DOC-4 (IP Licence Back / Transition Services, if applicable) executed.
                • Escrow Agreement executed (IP indemnity escrow funded).
                • §338(h)(10) or §336(e) election forms signed (if applicable) — retain for joint tax return filing.

   PHASE 5: POST-CLOSING RECORDATION & INTEGRATION (T+12 to T+26 weeks)
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Week 13–14: USPTO recordal — record all patent and trademark assignments (Electronic Assignment System). Priority: within 3 months of closing to preserve bona fide purchaser status (35 U.S.C. §261).
   Week 13–16: WIPO/national registry recordal — EP, PCT, national phase patents and international trademarks.
   Week 13–16: USCO recordal — copyright assignments for registered works.
   Week 14:    Domain name registrar transfers — update WHOIS registrant to Acquirer entity.
   Week 14:    Social media handle ownership transfer (platform-specific processes).
   Week 16:    Trade secret protocol implemented — new NDA templates, access controls, trade secret register updated to reflect Acquirer ownership.
   Week 20:    Post-closing OSS compliance programme established — SBOM integrated into Acquirer's CI/CD pipeline for ongoing licence monitoring.
   Week 26:    IP integration report delivered to deal team; confirm all recordals complete; confirm no outstanding assignment obligations.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PART VI — OPEN ITEMS & CONDITIONS PRECEDENT (IP)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

IP-014 CLOSING CONDITIONS — IP SPECIFIC

   The following IP conditions precedent must be satisfied prior to closing:

   (a) OSS CONDITION: No BLOCKED OSS components remain in any production or distributed codebase. IP Counsel to issue written OSS clearance certificate.
   (b) ASSIGNMENT CONDITION: All material assignment gaps identified in IP-005 have been cured by fully executed Confirmatory Assignments.
   (c) LICENCE CONSENT CONDITION: Written consent received from all Tier 1 licence counterparties identified in IP-006.
   (d) REGISTERED IP CONDITION: USPTO/WIPO/national registry searches confirm no undisclosed liens, security interests, or encumbrances on any registered IP asset.
   (e) GOVERNMENT FUNDING CONDITION: Target has confirmed in writing that no federal funding subject to Bayh-Dole Act (35 U.S.C. §§200–212) was used in development of any IP asset to be acquired, or alternatively, all Bayh-Dole obligations (invention disclosure, march-in rights) have been identified and disclosed.

IP-015 RISK FLAGS REQUIRING DEAL TEAM DECISION

   [The following items require instruction from deal team / business principals before IP Counsel can opine on acceptability:]

   RISK-A: [To be populated upon receipt of target IP materials — potential AGPL component in product stack]
   RISK-B: [To be populated — potential founder pre-incorporation IP not formally assigned]
   RISK-C: [To be populated — material inbound licence with change-of-control clause]

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SCHEDULES (TO BE COMPLETED UPON RECEIPT OF TARGET MATERIALS)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SCHEDULE A: IP Asset Valuation Support Schedule (§1060 / Form 8594 Class VI/VII)
SCHEDULE B: OSS Attribution Report & SBOM (SPDX 2.3 / CycloneDX 1.5)
SCHEDULE C: Registered IP Portfolio (Patents, Trademarks, Copyrights, Domains)
SCHEDULE D: Inbound Licence Matrix (Anti-Assignment Clause Analysis)
SCHEDULE E: Employee/Contractor Assignment Gap Register
SCHEDULE F: OSS Remediation Tracker (BLOCKED/FLAGGED Items & Status)
SCHEDULE G: Form of Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement (DOC-1)
SCHEDULE H: Form of Confirmatory Patent Assignment (DOC-2)
SCHEDULE I: Form of Invention Assignment & Confidentiality Agreement (DOC-3)

international registrations noted). Local IP counsel should be engaged
for material IP assets in non-U.S. jurisdictions (EU, UK, CN, JP, KR,

should confirm all §338/§336/§1060 elections with qualified tax counsel.
